text:
Mitch Marner's second season in Vegas reads exactly like his reputation: 20 points in 17 games, 17 of them assists. He stretched a point streak to ten games before Detroit shut him out on Nov. 5, then answered with a goal and an assist in Buffalo, the goal a shorthanded breakaway.

The assists are the reliable part. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him moving the puck out of his zone with possession 62% of the time and in the top fifth of forwards in primary shot assists. The goals are the soft spot: three on 41 shots is 7.3%, well under his usual 11 to 15%, and he is three goals short of what his chances suggest. That one should turn.

He skates in the bottom third of the league by top speed, which never mattered much for him; he wins with timing. Our projection has him around 82 points with 20 goals. If he gets back to shooting like himself, both numbers go up.
headline: Marner the passer, waiting on his shot
